title: Project Documentation & README
content:
## Overview

The project maintains a single `README.md` at the repo root as the authoritative source of documentation. Two previously existing extra README files (`README2.md`, `README3.md`) were deleted and their relevant content merged into `README.md`.

A `CLAUDE.md` file also exists at the repo root, providing project-level guidance for AI agents.

The README is periodically audited directly against the source code and test files (not written from memory), which is how stale or missing documentation gets caught and corrected.

---

## README.md

### Structure

The README is organized as:

- **Gameplay screenshot** — a real, in-game screenshot (`docs/screenshot.png`) sits at the very top of the README, above the headline description, giving visitors an immediate visual preview of the game
- **Headline description** — leads with the isometric 3D board and the expanding grid mechanic as the defining features of this snake implementation
- **Game modes section** — documents all four entry points (single player, two-player PvP, solo bot, bot-vs-bot) plus **Iron Snake Mode**
- **Bot strategy table** — covers all 11 bots
- **Controls table** — includes rotation, perspective toggle, overhead view, Enter, and Esc keys. Does **not** document a bot-autoplay toggle shortcut — that shortcut no longer exists in the code (the handler was removed) and its stale mention was removed from the README
- **Quick-start instructions** — covers both development and production builds
- **Testing section** — documents the Playwright test commands for the project's end-to-end test suite
- **Tech Stack** — includes an entry for the Playwright test framework alongside the rest of the stack
- **Coming soon section** — trimmed to only genuinely unshipped items
- **Project memory section** — at the bottom; describes Jolli Memory and links to `docs/jolli-memory/README-JOLLI-MEMORY.md`

### Gameplay screenshot

`docs/screenshot.png` now depicts an **Iron Snake Mode** board rather than a standard gameplay board. It was replaced because the previous hero image (a longer, standard-board gameplay shot) didn't showcase the game's more distinctive irregular-board mode, and a new screenshot was requested that specifically shows a non-square board with a visible interior hole.

The current image was captured using a temporary Playwright-based capture script (removed after use) that enabled Iron Snake mode, ran an automated bot, and progressed the game to level 2–3, where board holes are larger and more visible. The frame was taken right after the snake leveled up to level 3, while the snake was still short — this keeps the newly-formed hole unobstructed, since longer snakes tend to cover the board's interior. Because the board rotates automatically, roughly 26 frames were burst-captured across a full rotation so the best isometric angle could be chosen deliberately, rather than relying on a single lucky capture. The selected frame clearly shows both the irregular/notched board outline and an interior hole (a gap in the board surface, distinct from the yellow death marker).

The image is embedded at the top of `README.md`, and its alt text was updated to describe Iron Snake mode, the irregular board shape, the interior hole, and the level/goal HUD, replacing the older checkerboard-style description.

### Headline / distinctive features

The expanding grid mechanic and adjustable starting grid resolution are surfaced prominently as the most distinctive behaviors of this snake implementation compared to a standard clone. This sets expectations for evaluators and contributors.

### Shipped features (in main feature list)

- Isometric 3D board
- Two-player PvP mode
- Expanding grid with adjustable starting grid size
- High score persistence
- Pause/resume
- Dark theme
- **Iron Snake Mode** — irregular, randomly-shaped boards with interior holes, per-level score goals, and board reshaping between levels

Iron Snake Mode was shipped and playtested but had gone completely undocumented until an audit against the actual source and test files surfaced it; it is now described in both the feature list and the game modes section, and is additionally showcased visually via the README's hero screenshot.

### Intentionally undocumented

A hidden 🌈 rainbow-snake Easter egg exists in the code but is **deliberately left out of the README** so as not to spoil the surprise for players who might discover it on their own. It is not listed as "coming soon" because it is already implemented — it is simply undocumented by design, not unshipped.

An **Iron Snake exit-door mechanic** was found only on a separate, unmerged branch and is not present in the current codebase; it is correctly left undocumented as not-yet-shipped and is not part of the public roadmap until it lands on main.

### Coming soon (roadmap)

Only genuinely unimplemented items are listed here:

- Color blind mode (requested in user feedback; deduplicated to one entry)
- First-person view (user-requested: see the game from the snake's own perspective)
- Possible rename to "snek"
- Global/online leaderboard — distinct from the local per-mode leaderboards that already exist

### Project memory section

A "Project memory" section at the bottom of `README.md` provides a brief description of Jolli Memory and a relative link to `docs/jolli-memory/README-JOLLI-MEMORY.md`. The link was added by cherry-picking a single isolated commit onto a fresh branch built on top of the already-updated main (rather than reusing an older local branch based on stale history), keeping the resulting PR diff limited to just the link addition and avoiding merge conflicts with the already-merged guide content.

The purpose of the section is discoverability: without it, the Jolli Memory guide was present in the repo but invisible to anyone browsing the project.

---

## CLAUDE.md

Created in commit `7fdbb7ae`. Contains a **"Use Jolli Memory"** section instructing Claude to:

- Recall prior branch context before planning or coding
- Search across branches when design questions arise
- Use the Jolli PR skill when opening pull requests

### Why a project-level file

A project-level guidance file is loaded into context every session and applies to anyone working in the repo. A memory entry would not be reliably loaded; a hook would be too rigid for a "when relevant" guideline and would misfire on unrelated tasks.

---

## Content consolidation decisions

- `README2.md` and `README3.md` were deleted; their content was merged into the "Coming soon" section of `README.md`
- `README3.md` originally held raw user feedback (color blind mode, viewing other players' high scores, first-person view) recorded verbatim without product decisions; these were triaged into the roadmap on merge
- Redundant framing (separate "future plans" and "user feedback" headers) was dropped rather than preserved as subsections
- The overlapping color blind mode request that appeared in both deleted files was deduplicated to a single roadmap entry
- Global leaderboards were explicitly re-added to the roadmap (not dropped) because they represent a genuine user request distinct from existing local leaderboards
- The Jolli Memory guide link was added to the main README rather than left undiscoverable, so repo visitors know the guide exists
- The README's hero screenshot was replaced with an Iron Snake Mode board (irregular shape, visible interior hole) instead of a standard gameplay board, to better showcase the game's most distinctive mode; the frame was chosen from a burst of ~26 captures across the board's automatic rotation, taken just after a level-up while the snake was still short so the hole stayed unobstructed
- Documentation audits are done by verifying every claim (grid size limits, level-up thresholds, keyboard shortcuts, shipped mechanics) against actual source and test files rather than editing from memory
